      "sentence": "The patient has severe hypotension and cold, clammy skin, with decreased cardiac output and elevated pulmonary capillary wedge pressure.",

    {
      "sentence": "Low cardiac output despite elevated left-sided filling pressure indicates cardiogenic shock.",
      "grounding": "none",

    },
    {
      "sentence": "Myocardial infarction, tachyarrhythmias, and severe aortic stenosis can all reduce cardiac output.",

      "passage_ids": ["Neurology_Adams:002191"]
    },
    {
      "sentence": "Acute myocardial infarction can impair ventricular contraction, rapid atrial fibrillation can impair ventricular filling, and severe valvular stenosis can limit forward flow, making I, II, and IV the correct combination.",
      "grounding": "none",
      "question_quote": null,
      "passage_ids": []
    },
    {
      "sentence": "Massive pulmonary embolism instead causes obstructive shock with a typically normal or low wedge pressure, while hemorrhage and sepsis classically cause hypovolemic and distributive shock, respectively.",
